claims.statement: OpenHands is a community-driven platform for developing AI agents that interact with the world through software interfaces (code execution, command line, web browsing).
confidence_reasons: Multiple design choices support this claim

claims.statement: CodeActAgent v1.8 with claude-3.5-sonnet reaches a 26.0% resolve rate on SWE-Bench Lite (300 instances, without hint text).
Model choice produces a large difference in SWE-Bench Lite performance: claude-3.5-sonnet (26.0%) versus gpt-4o-mini (6.3%), a 19.7 percentage-point gap under otherwise identical conditions.
claims.scope: SWE-Bench Lite performance variance across models
confidence_reasons: Controlled conditions differ only by model

claims.statement: CodeActAgent v1.5 fixes 79.3% of bugs on the HumanEvalFix Python subset (164 instances) using a 0-shot, multi-turn self-debugging setup.
On HumanEvalFix, CodeActAgent's 0-shot result is reported by the authors as better than non-agentic approaches and close to double the pass rate of StarCoder2-15B.
confidence_reasons: Based on a single measured result
Comparison baseline values not included in the evidence package

claims.statement: The same CodeActAgent, without any change to its system prompt, is evaluated across software-engineering, web-browsing, and miscellaneous-assistance tasks.
confidence_reasons: Multiple evidence points from different benchmarks
Same agent configuration used across categories

claims.statement: On the 812-instance WebArena benchmark, BrowsingAgent v1.0 scores between 8.5% and 15.5% depending on the underlying model, using domain-general zero-shot prompting.
On the 198-question GPQA diamond set, CodeActAgent v1.8 with claude-3.5-sonnet reaches 52.0% accuracy, compared with 81.3% for expert humans and 38.8% for GPT-4 with search.
confidence_reasons: Baseline comparison provided in the same table

claims.statement: On the 225-instance MINT math subset, CodeActAgent v1.5 with gpt-4o reaches 77.3% with up to five rounds of tool/feedback interaction.
On the 600-instance challenging (5-hop) ProofWriter subset, CodeActAgent v1.5 reaches 78.8% accuracy.
OpenHands integrates 15 established benchmarks spanning software engineering (7), web browsing (2), and miscellaneous assistance (6).
At the time of writing, OpenHands had received 32K GitHub stars and more than 2.1K contributions from over 188 contributors.
The authors report that current agents still struggle with complex tasks, particularly editing long files.
confidence_reasons: Explicitly stated limitation by the authors

claims.statement: Constructing new agent workflows in OpenHands currently requires substantial handcrafted engineering effort.
The authors state that OpenHands is intended to help identify and address the risks of increasingly capable agents by enabling systematic evaluation before wide deployment.
confidence_reasons: Stated as a goal/hypothesis rather than a demonstrated result

claims.statement: The full MiniWoB++ evaluation set (125 environments) includes tasks that require vision capability to solve.
confidence_reasons: Explicit statement in the methods text

claims.statement: For BIRD, the authors extended the standard single-turn setting to allow multi-turn interaction so the agent can revise a SQL query using execution feedback.
OpenHands' Docker-based runtime uses a dual-tagging scheme (a hash-based tag for reproducibility and a generic tag for the latest version) to balance reproducibility with flexibility.
OpenHands' integration-test framework mocks LLM calls with predefined responses keyed to exact prompt matches, enabling deterministic tests without incurring live LLM costs.
confidence_reasons: Explicit technical description of the testing approach

claims.statement: Running the full SWE-Bench evaluation (2294 instances) is estimated by the authors to cost approximately $6.9k under a conservative per-instance estimate, which is why the smaller SWE-Bench Lite (300 instances) is used for most reported results.
confidence_reasons: Soft evidence: a footnote estimate, not a logged expenditure

limitations.statement: Agent performance depends strongly on the underlying LLM: on SWE-Bench Lite, claude-3.5-sonnet outperforms gpt-4o-mini by roughly 4x (26.0% vs 6.3%).
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Claims about OpenHands' 'competitive performance' hold for specific model backends and should not be read as model-independent.

limitations.statement: Many results are reported on reduced-size benchmark subsets (e.g., SWE-Bench Lite's 300 instances rather than the full 2294-instance SWE-Bench) for cost reasons.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Reported rates may not transfer unchanged to the full benchmarks; evaluation scope is bounded by cost.

limitations.statement: Agents built on OpenHands still struggle with complex tasks and with editing long files.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Practical applicability to complex, real-world software-engineering tasks is limited by current agent capability, not just platform design.

limitations.statement: Building new agent workflows in OpenHands still requires substantial handcrafted engineering.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Claims about ease of extending OpenHands to new agents are bounded: the framework does not yet automate workflow construction.

limitations.statement: HumanEvalFix allows a theoretical maximum of 100%, so 79.3% is not a ceiling result.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: There is room for improvement; 79.3% reflects a capability gap rather than a benchmark limit.

limitations.statement: The full MiniWoB++ evaluation set includes vision-dependent tasks.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Web-browsing scores that include the full MiniWoB++ set partly reflect multimodal (vision) capability, not only browsing-action competence.

negative_result_decisions.reason: Demonstrates model sensitivity and guides model selection for practitioners; important for reproducibility.
